column1: # Latin key <TAB> Devanagari word — hand-written, merged into the word list FST
# Why this file exists separately from the generated list: mkwords.py derives
# each key by inverting the Devanagari spelling through the schema, which is
# right for Nepali words and useless for these. Nobody reaches कम्प्युटर by
# typing `kamPyuTar`; they type `computer`, English spelling and all, and the
# rule engine reads that letter by letter into चोम्पुतेर — a form so far from
# the word that no amount of fuzzy re-ranking gets back. The same goes for place
# names with a settled English spelling: `kathmandu`, not `kaaThamaaDauM`.
# So: the key is what a person types, the value is what they meant. Where usage
# is genuinely split, list both keys. Order does not matter; build.rs sorts.
# Groups: English loanwords, then Nepali places, then the wider world, then
# names. All in their accepted Nepali spelling — नेपाली orthography, not Hindi.
# ---- everyday words the generated lexicon simply does not have ---------------
# nep_dict is a lexicon rather than a word list and skips ordinary vocabulary;
# `data/extra-ne.txt` is the hatch for that, but it only takes effect when
# mkwords.py is re-run against the source database. These are the ones the
